questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-14t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}-147t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
When is the particle momentarily at rest?

options.why: Kept the negative root of $3t^{2}=147$ even though the motion is restricted to $t\ge 0$.
Assumed the particle starts at rest without checking that $\dot{x}(0)=-14$, which is not zero.
Solved $2t-14=0$ as $t=14$ by adding $14$ instead of dividing by $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-14)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}-147)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$2t-14=0$
$t=7$
$3t^{2}-147=0$
$t^{2}=49$
$t=7$ (rejecting $t=-7$ since $t\ge 0$)
Both components vanish at $t=7$, so the particle is at rest only at $t=7$.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-12t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(5t+2)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
At what time is the particle moving parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$?

options.why: Solved $3t^{2}=12$ as $t=4$ by dividing only once instead of taking the square root.
Kept the negative root of $t^{2}=4$ even though the motion is restricted to $t\ge 0$.
Set $\dot{y}=0$ instead of $\dot{x}=0$; since $\dot{y}=5$ is never zero this wrongly rules the situation out.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(3t^{2}-12)\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$
Moving parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$ means $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}\ne 0$.
$3t^{2}-12=0$
$t^{2}=4$
$t=2$ (rejecting $t=-2$ since $t\ge 0$)
$\dot{y}=5\ne 0$, so the particle moves parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$ at $t=2$.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-8t)\underset{\sim}{i}+6t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
What is its minimum speed?

options.why: Assumed that $\dot{x}=0$ makes the particle stop, but $\dot{y}=6$ is never zero.
Evaluated the speed at $t=0$, $\sqrt{64+36}$, instead of finding where the speed is least.
Minimised $\dot{x}+\dot{y}=2t-2$ instead of $\sqrt{\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}}$; a speed can never be negative.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-8)\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=(2t-8)^{2}+36$
The square root is increasing, so the speed is least when $(2t-8)^{2}$ is least.
$(2t-8)^{2}=0$
$t=4$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(4)|$
$=\sqrt{0+36}$
$=6$

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-9t^{2}+15t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-10t+25)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Where is the particle at the instant it is momentarily at rest?

options.why: Used $t=1$, which makes only $\dot{x}$ zero, without checking $\dot{y}(1)=-8$.
Evaluated $125-225+75$ as $+25$ instead of $-25$.
Quoted the velocity at the rest time, which is the zero vector, instead of the position.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(3t^{2}-18t+15)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-10)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$3(t-1)(t-5)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=5$
$2t-10=0$
$t=5$
Both components vanish only at $t=5$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(5)$
$=(125-225+75)\underset{\sim}{i}+(25-50+25)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-25\underset{\sim}{i}+0\underset{\sim}{j}$

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}-48t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Which statement about the motion is correct?

options.text: It is never at rest; at $t=3$ it moves parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$ and at $t=4$ it moves parallel to $\underset{\sim}{i}$.
It is never at rest; at $t=3$ it moves parallel to $\underset{\sim}{i}$ and at $t=4$ it moves parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$.
options.why: Swapped the two directions: $\dot{x}=0$ leaves only a j component, so the motion there is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$.

options.text: It is at rest at $t=3$, and at $t=4$ it moves parallel to $\underset{\sim}{i}$.
options.why: Treated $\dot{x}=0$ on its own as being at rest, without requiring $\dot{y}=0$ at the same time.

options.text: It is at rest at $t=3$ and again at $t=4$.
options.why: Treated each component vanishing separately as a rest time; at rest needs both components zero together.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}-48)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
$3t^{2}-48=0$
$t^{2}=16$
$t=4$ (rejecting $t=-4$ since $t\ge 0$)
The components are never zero together, so the particle is never at rest.
At $t=3$ only $\dot{x}=0$, so the velocity is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$; at $t=4$ only $\dot{y}=0$, so the velocity is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{i}$.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=2\cos 3t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+7t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $0<t\le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
At what time is the particle moving parallel to $\underset{\sim}{j}$?

options.why: Set $\cos 3t=0$ instead of $\sin 3t=0$, giving $3t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Solved $\sin 3t=0$ to get $3t=\pi$ but then wrote $t=\pi$ without dividing by $3$.
Included $3t=2\pi$, which gives $t=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, outside the stated interval $t\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=-6\sin 3t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\dot{y}=7$, which is never zero.
$-6\sin 3t=0$
For $0<t\le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $3t$ runs from $0$ to $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.
$3t=\pi$
$t=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{3}-21t^{2}+60t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-10t+3)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
When is the particle momentarily at rest?

options.why: Took a root of $\dot{x}=0$ without checking whether $\dot{y}$ is also zero there; $\dot{y}(2)=-6$.
Listed every root of $\dot{x}=0$ and treated them all as rest times.

options.text: The particle is never at rest
options.why: Mis-factorised $6t^{2}-42t+60$ and so found no time shared with the root of $\dot{y}=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(6t^{2}-42t+60)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-10)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$6(t-2)(t-5)=0$
$t=2$ or $t=5$
$2t-10=0$
$t=5$
Both components vanish only at $t=5$, so the particle is at rest at $t=5$.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t^{2}+4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$, with distances in metres and $t$ in seconds.
What is its minimum speed?

options.why: Assumed the particle must come to rest somewhere; here $\dot{x}=0$ at $t=1$ but $\dot{y}(1)=8$.
Added $|\dot{x}|$ and $|\dot{y}|$ at $t=0$ instead of using $\sqrt{\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}}$.
Used only the j component of the velocity at $t=0$ and ignored the i component.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(4t+4)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=(2t-2)^{2}+(4t+4)^{2}$
$=4t^{2}-8t+4+16t^{2}+32t+16$
$=20t^{2}+24t+20$
The vertex of this parabola is at $t=-\dfrac{24}{40}=-0.6$, which is outside $t\ge 0$.
So $20t^{2}+24t+20$ is increasing on $t\ge 0$ and is least at $t=0$.
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(0)|$
$=\sqrt{20}$
$=2\sqrt{5}$ m/s

questions.question_text:
A particle starts from a fixed position $O$ with velocity $(\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
It travels with constant acceleration $(-2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.
What is its speed after 4 seconds?

options.why: Gives the final velocity vector rather than its scalar speed.
Applies the acceleration components incorrectly over four seconds.
Uses an incorrect magnitude after combining velocity and acceleration.

questions.solution_text: After 4 seconds, $\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at=(\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)+4(-2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)=-7\mathbf i+7\mathbf j$. Its speed is $|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{(-7)^2+7^2}=7\sqrt2\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
